Compound SNBL — Case Study: Building the Product Behind Save Now, Buy Later
Omar Mostafa Mohaseb was Product Lead & Consultant at Compound (part-time, remote, Mar–Dec 2025). Compound is a UAE/MENA fintech built on Save Now, Buy Later (SNBL) — the structural opposite of BNPL.

Instead of: buy now → pay later → debt
Compound: save first → earn merchant-funded rewards → purchase debt-free

Omar joined after the initial concept was defined. His scope covered execution: consumer savings journey (goal creation through redemption), customer dashboard, embeddable merchant widget and merchant onboarding, admin backoffice portal, API documentation, and a mobile app prototype built using Claude Code and Cursor.

Four core surfaces shipped: consumer mobile app, embeddable checkout widget, admin backoffice portal, API documentation.

The SNBL Thesis and Market Position
Compound's thesis: consumers want the outcome of BNPL (large purchases they can't immediately afford) without the debt mechanism. The market segment is consumers motivated by financial discipline rather than deferred payment.

Four hypotheses:
1. People want the outcome of BNPL, not the debt — the desire for the purchase is real; the resistance is to the repayment obligation
2. Many purchases are planned — travel, electronics, furniture, education, car down payments have natural 3-6 month purchase timelines that map onto savings plans
3. Brands will fund rewards if it lowers CAC — a customer who saves for 3 months before purchasing is more committed than one who clicks an ad; merchant-funded rewards make the economics work
4. Commitment before purchase predicts retention — pre-purchase saving creates an engagement period with the brand before the transaction

Unique market position: most fintech competes on credit (better, faster, cheaper). Compound competes on the absence of credit. Compound's tagline: 'Save now. Shop smarter.'

The Embedded Widget as Distribution Strategy
Compound's highest-leverage product decision: not a consumer app feature, but a distribution strategy.

Two options evaluated:
Option A — Drive consumers to the Compound app: acquire through marketing, let them discover merchants from inside the platform. Problem: requires owning the discovery moment before purchase intent exists. High marketing cost.
Option B — Bring Compound to merchants: embeddable JavaScript widget that merchants install on their landing pages, e-commerce sites, clinic sites, travel agency booking flows. Consumers encounter SNBL at the point where purchase intent already exists.

Decision: Option B. The widget is the distribution mechanism.

Widget flow: Consumer lands on merchant site → sees Compound widget → starts a savings goal for that product → deposits over time → returns to merchant to redeem.

The widget turns merchant traffic into savings commitments, and savings commitments into high-intent future purchases. Distribution was embedded at the point of purchase intent, not at the point of Compound discovery.

Consumer Journey, Merchant Journey, and AI Prototyping

Consumer journey (5 steps): Goal creation (select merchant, set target and timeline) → Funding (initial deposit + recurring contributions) → Progress tracking (dashboard: savings, rewards, purchase readiness %) → Rewards accumulation (merchant-funded, earned while saving) → Redemption (goal reached → voucher/code → purchase)

Merchant journey: Signup and verification → Merchant dashboard (campaign management, savings activity, conversion tracking) → Reward configuration (how much merchants fund per goal, at what milestones) → Widget installation (zero-friction JS snippet) → Campaign monitoring (active savers, goal completion, redemptions, revenue)

AI-Assisted Mobile App Prototyping:
Omar used Claude Code and Cursor to prototype the Compound customer mobile app before handoff to engineering. The prototype covered core flows: goal creation, funding, progress tracking, dashboard. Benefits: compressed iteration from weeks to days, engineering alignment via interactive reference rather than static spec, resource efficiency (validate decisions before consuming engineering cycles).

PM lesson: AI-assisted prototyping produces decision-quality artifacts that make engineering conversations more precise. It's a PM workflow, not just a developer tool.
